_comment_type: NOT a syllabus-based course. Per the source page this is an annual SUBSCRIPTION to a growing library of standalone, production-grade projects spanning AI/ML, Data Science, GenAI, Agentic AI and Data Engineering/MLOps, plus live project-walkthrough sessions. There is no single curriculum, no cohort, and no named module list — only project categories and a shared project-design template. module_groups below reflects that: it clusters the source's stated project categories and design methodology, not a lecture syllabus.

_comment_title: Copied verbatim from the checkout page, including its irregular spacing/punctuation ('Gen AI/Agentic AI/ DE', no space before the parenthesis) per §1's copy-exactly rule for title.
_comment_overview: PARAPHRASED from the sponsor's checkout page — never copy marketing prose verbatim. Facts (yearly subscription, five project domains, alternate-weekend live sessions, Krish Naik Academy) are used as-is; the 'bridges the gap' / 'toy datasets vs real company environments' framing is rewritten rather than quoted.
overview: An annual subscription from Krish Naik Academy giving access to a growing library of standalone, production-grade projects across AI/ML, Data Science, Generative AI, Agentic AI, and Data Engineering/MLOps, rather than a single fixed syllabus. Each project follows the same industry-style template — problem framing, system architecture, data pipelines, model or agent development, deployment-ready implementation, and evaluation — with new projects added throughout the subscription period. Alternate Saturday and Sunday evening sessions provide project walkthroughs and doubt clarification alongside the self-paced project library.
_comment_category: JUDGMENT CALL. The page names five equally-weighted domains (AI/ML, Data Science, GenAI, Agentic AI, Data Engineering & MLOps), so no domain is textually dominant. Primary is set to MLOps/LLMOps because that is what actually differentiates THIS service from the catalog's teaching bootcamps: unlike e.g. ultimate-data-science-ai-engineering-3-0, this page teaches no fundamentals (no Python/stats/DL modules) and its entire pitch is deployment-grade engineering practice — 'production-level', 'scalable', 'deployment-ready implementation', 'real deployment scenarios', 'architecture diagrams'. Data Science, GenAI/LLM Engineering, Agentic AI and Data Engineering are all carried as secondaries so the diversity cap (B3) still sees the full span.
_comment_level: Page targets 'Aspiring Data Scientists, ML Engineers, AI Engineers', professionals 'transitioning into' GenAI/Agentic AI roles, and learners wanting 'industry exposure beyond courses' — i.e. people who already have foundational knowledge and want applied, production-grade practice, not first-time learners. No beginner track is offered anywhere on the page, so beginner is excluded from level_range. `level`=intermediate is the fusion anchor; level_range is stored only, not scored (§1).
_comment_price: Page shows a struck-through ₹12000 list price and a current ₹9000/yearly price. Stored the current effective price (₹9000) as the number a buyer actually pays today, matching how other own-site Krish Naik Academy pages in this catalog store the displayed price rather than a list price. Band 'mid' per §2 (₹3,000-9,999). This is own-site fixed pricing, not Udemy coupon pricing, so a number (not null) is appropriate here — but the visible markdown means it could move; re-check at re-curation.
_comment_rating: No star rating or review count published on the page. Null, not guessed — the validator's null-rating warning is expected.

format._comment_mode: 'hybrid' because the offering is BOTH a durable, always-available project library (start any project today) AND scheduled live sessions (project walkthroughs and doubt clarification, alternate Sat & Sun). Not 'self-paced' because live sessions are explicitly part of delivery; not 'live' because there is no single cohort start — access begins on purchase.
format._comment_cohort_start: No cohort exists for a rolling-enrollment subscription — this is a structural null, not a stale-past-date case like the sibling bootcamp files. No next cohort to record. Per §6 this still demotes the freshness mode prior toward 'recorded' (0.45) in the absence of a future date, which is an accurate reflection of what freshness.py can determine from a subscription with no time-bound intake.

format._comment_duration_hours: Null by design — the project library is open-ended and growing throughout the subscription; no total content-hours figure is published.

format._comment_dates: No publish date, 'last updated' badge, or version string is published, and none is implied by a stable module list since the library is explicitly described as growing. All three left null per §7 rather than guessed; recency falls through to the unknown floor (0.35, §6).
